name: Mind maps
intro: Where nodes are quick to create and sync never loses the map, and where it is a stripped-down mobile app.

apps.title: Xmind: AI Mind Map, Brainstorm
apps.verdict: XMind is one of the most fully developed mind map editors out there. It offers a rich library of diagram types (fishbone, matrix, timeline), elegant themes, and fast node entry. The main pain point is cross-platform sync, which is unreliable, and the Vision Pro version breaks after updates. AI features were added, but some users find them unnecessary.
apps.loved: Multiple diagram formats in one editor: you switch from a classic map to a matrix or fishbone with a single click, without rebuilding the structure by hand.
apps.weak: Sync between devices works through manual export and import rather than live cloud sync. A map opened on iPad cannot be continued on Mac without re-saving the file.
apps.whoFor: STEM students and analysts who need one tool for different structure types and are willing to pay a subscription for the breadth of formats.

quotes.text: There is no syncing feature in this app, and I'm not sure why. It seems with the ability to collaborate on a mind map, I should also be able to seamlessly work on a map on my iPad, then when I get home, be able to work on it on my desktop without needing to manually upload then download using a 3rd
I would've given it 5-star rating if it had supported synchronization among different platforms.
Exporting as a jpg or a png fails to load, like the file is corrupted. I did have success with a PDF export, though.

Got the free trial in hopes of making mind maps in preparation for my studies (I'm a STEM grad student). This app really is designed for small bits of information not complex biochemical concepts. It's a good idea in practice, but it does need a lot of work. I think there was 10? templates and no sh

i have a very autonomous job, which i love, but i have such a hard time organizing my tasks and figuring it what order to do them in because of my adhd. I decided to try mind mapping, and i NEEDED something that worked on my ipad, as well as both my personal and work computers that run windows.

apps.title: SimpleMind Pro - Mind Mapping
apps.verdict: A mature one-time-purchase mind mapper with a rich set of layouts and support for non-linear connections. Valued for no subscription and fast performance. Main pain points are the absence of iCloud Drive and unreliable sync through third-party services. The select tool is awkward for bulk node selection.
apps.loved: Support for non-linear connections (not just parent-child). Many layout options. Fast even on large maps. Available on iOS, macOS, and Windows with a shared file format. No monthly subscription.
apps.weak: No native iCloud Drive support, only Dropbox and Google Drive. Sync between devices fails periodically. Selecting multiple nodes requires deselecting before each new one, which is frustrating for bulk formatting. Images are automatically compressed to low quality.
apps.whoFor: Writers, researchers, or students who need a serious mind map tool without a subscription and with cross-platform support.

quotes.text: This is the best and easiest to use tool until you want share your work across devices. No iCloud support? Ridiculous.

I was looking for a mind map app that showed for non hierarchical relationships (so not just parent-child) and that didn't require a subscription and this has proved to be excellent. App is very fast, and good for taking notes on books, timelines of history, plotting out systems.
I was sad to no longer have iThoughts on my iPad and I'm very happy to have found this powerful alternative.

I'm relatively new to mind mapping and didn't want to try the other versions because of either their lack of cross-platform support or subscription model. I purchased this app for macOS, iPadOS, and windows. It works similarly and equally well on each.
There are multiple bugs that have not been resolved. The most damaging is the sync bug, I'll work on iPad at home then when I need the info when at work it is not on my iPhone.

apps.title: SimpleMind - Mind Mapping
apps.verdict: SimpleMind is a fast and reliable mind map editor with a one-time purchase instead of a subscription. It supports multiple map formats (bubbles, timeline, vertical), and runs smoothly even on older iPads. The main drawback is no handwriting input with Apple Pencil, the stylus only replaces touch input without handwriting recognition.
apps.loved: One-time purchase with no subscription: pay once and own the editor forever, which sets it sharply apart from competitors with annual plans.
apps.weak: Apple Pencil does not recognize handwritten text in nodes. The stylus works only as a finger substitute, so handwritten notes directly on the map are not possible.
apps.whoFor: Solo users and students who need a fast, reliable thinking tool without a subscription and without extra features.

quotes.text: SimpleMind you are good. You have a lot going for you. But you are not as good as my beloved iThoughts yet. You lack the simple keyboard navigation to expand and condense nodes (or topics), and you lack the keyboard based resizing of the map to zoom in and out with ease.

For the paid app: I was looking for a mind map app that showed for non hierarchical relationships (so not just parent-child) and that didn't require a subscription and this has proved to be excellent.
However, they have no support for Apple Pencil except as a replacement for your finger.

apps.title: miMind - Mind Map, Brainstorm
apps.verdict: A functional mind mapper with a one-time purchase, quick-access buttons, and solid connection management between nodes. It lags noticeably behind modern competitors in design and UX. Cross-platform sync works, but the per-platform payment model frustrates loyal users.
apps.loved: Quick buttons for adding nodes without extra taps. Flexible connection management between any nodes, not only parent-child ones. Handles large maps (500+ nodes). Developers respond and fix bugs.
apps.weak: Bluetooth keyboard does not work for text input, which kills fast typing. Apple Pencil is not supported. The interface looks dated. Zoom on Mac works only through buttons, not the trackpad. Each platform requires a separate purchase.
apps.whoFor: Analysts or developers who need large maps with arbitrary connections and a one-time payment without a subscription.

quotes.text: Doesn't work with my bluetooth keyboard making it kind of useless to me. I was so excited to keep using it too….

Its a very good mind mapping piece of software. I feel you've got a lot of control over how the data is presented, and its much better than many other min map software for linking nodes/elements together.
Great app but would like pencil support
My biggest complaints are: Couldn't find the way to switch the template in existing map
I have a map in in form of outline... I couldn't find the way to switch the template in existing map

apps.title: Mind Mapping - MindMeister
apps.verdict: MindMeister is a mature cloud mind mapper with real-time collaboration and a clean interface. Undo is unreliable: two or three steps back can erase a node's text instead of restoring it. Map sync between devices sometimes breaks and loses data.
apps.loved: Collaborative editing: multiple people edit the map at the same time, changes appear instantly without refresh, which makes it convenient for team brainstorming.
apps.weak: Undo behaves unpredictably. After two or three steps back the app can wipe out a node's text instead of restoring the previous state.
apps.whoFor: Teams that need a quick collaborative brainstorm without complex structures and can tolerate unreliable undo.

quotes.text: I paid for export capability and the image export only gives a 500 internal server error.
Cannot organize and move freely mindmaps the way I want and need to.
It doesn't always sync well across devices, and sometimes I lose maps and data.

apps.title: Lucidchart
apps.verdict: Lucidchart is a powerful web service for flowcharts and diagrams with a rich shape library and collaboration. The mobile app is effectively dead for solo users: the company restricted it to Team and Enterprise plans. Productively strong, but it has strategically abandoned its individual user base.
apps.loved: Cross-platform collaboration: multiple participants edit a diagram at the same time, see each other's cursors, and leave comments directly on the canvas.
apps.weak: The mobile app is unavailable on individual plans. Users with annual subscriptions are forced to open a browser on their phone instead of using a native client.
apps.whoFor: Teams that need to collaboratively draw complex architectural or business diagrams and are paying for a corporate plan.

quotes.text: You removed my ability to use the iPad app even with a PAID account. There for, you lost a 5+ year paid user. Horrible decision you made, and you blame Apple for hurting your loyal customers, when the decision was yours.
I've used a few apps, this is the best one I've used that's truly cross platform, web, Mac, PC, iOS.
I've been using Lucid for years and constraining tablets and mobile now to teams/organization and removing the application from supporting individual (paid) account was a terrible decision.

apps.title: Mind Map Maker - Mindomo
apps.verdict: A full-featured cross-platform mind mapper with templates and a web version, but the mobile app is noticeably weaker than the web in features. Nodes move in jerks and snapping breaks the layout. Apple Pencil support is rough.
apps.loved: Works across multiple platforms with synced data. Templates help you start without a blank slate. Free navigation without a required hierarchy appeals to users who build non-linear maps.
apps.weak: Dragging nodes on mobile is jumpy and snapping is chaotic. The mobile version lacks many web features: no floating topics, no outline conversion, no links between separate maps. Keyboard shortcuts are absent.
apps.whoFor: A student or educator who already works with Mindomo on the web and occasionally wants to open a map from their phone, not build one from scratch.

quotes.text: I really thought this was going to be the app! Unless I'm mistaken though, there are no keyboard shortcuts? To quickly brainstorm, I have to be able to mind map without touching the screen. If there aren't keyboard shortcuts implemented, I can't really use it.
I've been testing your app for about a week now and I'm having issues with sharing my map.. Sending it as a pdf in an email doesn't send the included pictures in a box.
Often more frustrating to use than helpful. You can't do half of what you can on the web version or it is at least very unclear how to
In trying to use my Apple Pencil for text input it caused nodes to drag, to disappear, or didn't actually write. I'm going to try to find an alternative.
The templates are helpful tools, and it is also very simple to create your own maps.
There is no option for converting an existing mind map to outline format
When you move blocks, the motion is jittery and it snaps to the most random places
The offline mode seems to work with pretty good syncing once back online

apps.title: AYOA - Mind Mapping
apps.verdict: AYOA (formerly iMindMap, formerly DropTask) has a tangled history: it started as a mind map tool by Tony Buzan, then task management was added, and now both coexist. The mobile client lags far behind the web version: some features are unavailable, Apple Pencil performs poorly, and new users often hit a white screen on first launch.
apps.loved: A visually organic map in the signature iMindMap style: branches are curved and hand-drawn rather than straight lines. The map looks like a real mind map, not a flowchart.
apps.weak: The mobile client is a stripped-down copy of the web version. Menus and features available in the browser are missing in the app, and users discover this only after buying a subscription.
apps.whoFor: Users who value the organic visual style of classic iMindMap and are comfortable working primarily through the web version.

quotes.text: The iOS Ayoa application is not ready primetime use. No clear way to clean up a Map. Navigation with the Apple Pencil is poor. Most of the menu options available in the web application are not available.
We have been a paying client for 4 years now with 25 employees. The software is great for tasks and projects.

apps.title: Mind Mapping
apps.verdict: A visually polished mind mapper with smooth input UX, but the free tier is deliberately capped at 10 nodes. Any real topic exceeds that limit. Without paid access the tool is practically useless for serious work.
apps.loved: Smooth node input with an intuitive interface and no learning curve. A rich selection of themes and color schemes. Users switching from MindMeister appreciate the more flexible branching.
apps.weak: The 10-node limit on the free version makes the tool unworkable for any non-trivial task. The app crashes with many changes and does not save work. Portrait-only mode on iPad is a serious constraint for wide maps.
apps.whoFor: Someone willing to pay for a subscription right away and interested in building small, tidy maps on their phone.

apps.title: VisualMind: AI MindMap/Chatbot
apps.verdict: VisualMind generates a mind map from an AI prompt, but the map depth is limited to two levels, manual node editing barely works, and exports do not open for recipients. The concept is right, the execution is rough.
apps.loved: Fast start via AI prompt: enter a topic and get a draft map in seconds, without manually entering the first branches.
apps.weak: The map is built to two levels and stops there. Adding a third level of nesting or moving a branch is not possible. The structure is set by AI and cannot be changed by the user.
apps.whoFor: Anyone who wants to quickly visualize one idea on a single screen and does not plan to deepen or edit the map.

quotes.text: Please consider following suggestion: include an option to multi-select branches, sub-branches to be able to move items around. It is very frustrating to spend much time rearranging out of place branches.
I like this app, however when I try to share the mind map picture that's made out. People have trouble opening it.
